New innovations in HIV prevention could dramatically reduce the number of new HIV cases around the globe, but US foreign aid cuts will mean that those that most need the new medication will be unable to access it, according to experts at the Aids 2026 Conference in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

One year ago, the World Health Organization recommended that governments around the world prioritize expanded access to lenacapavir, an injectable version of the HIV prevention medication PrEP that requires only two injections annually. The heir to one of Malta’s biggest fortunes, Fenech is on trial for murder, accused of commissioning and paying for Caruana Galizia’s killing in a car bombing in October 2017.

Continue reading...

events.title: Middle East crisis live: Rubio hopes US can reach Hormuz deal with Iran ‘very shortly’ as officials say progress has been made
events.summary:
US secretary of state comments come after treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said Washington could reach a deal ‘by tomorrow’

  • US and Qatar report progress on Iran ceasefire and reopening Hormuz strait

Iran and Oman have made progress toward a deal to reopen the strait of Hormuz, a potential breakthrough that could help end the war in the Middle East, regional officials have said.

Under the emerging agreement, ships would enter the Persian Gulf through an Iranian-controlled route and exit through a route controlled by Oman, with service fees charged for providing security and preserving the maritime environment, two regional officials told the Associated Press.

Continue reading...

events.title: Iran’s president denies threatening to resign during talks over strait of Hormuz
events.summary:
Masoud Pezeshkian dismisses talk of internal rift as hardline Assembly of Experts call US negotiations ‘futile’

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

Masoud Pezeshkian, Iran’s president, has been forced to deny claims that he has repeatedly threatened to resign as he battles hardline factions opposed to reaching a settlement with the US over the strait of Hormuz.

The US and Europe hope a deal is imminent to reopen the strait and they are putting pressure on Oman to accept a temporary agreement that officials in Muscat fear will leave Iran retaining near permanent dominance of the vital oil shipping channel. Ships would enter the strait in a route close to Iran, but leave on a route that passes through Iranian and Omani waters.

Continue reading...

events.title: Mass funeral held in Gaza for victims of 2023 Israeli strike
events.summary:
Remains of 112 victims, including 40 children, recovered from rubble more than two years after residential block was destroyed

Mourners gathered in central Gaza on Tuesday for a mass funeral for 112 people, including 40 children, who were killed in 2023 in one of the deadliest Israeli strikes of the Gaza war.

Their bodies could not be recovered until now because of Israel’s continuing strikes, which have slowed, though not halted, since the ceasefire in October.

Continue reading...

events.title: US and Qatar report progress on Iran ceasefire and reopening Hormuz strait
events.summary:
Optimism echoes Trump’s claims on Monday that deal is close as mediators say they are exchanging proposals

  • Middle East crisis live – latest updates

US and Qatari officials have said progress is being made in restoring a ceasefire in the US-Iran war and reopening the strait of Hormuz.

The optimistic speculation on Tuesday brought oil prices down 2%, but the strait remained closed to shipping and a cargo vessel was reportedly struck by an unidentified projectile off Oman’s coast close to the strait.

Continue reading...

events.title: Elon Musk’s X latest to block Saudi dissident accounts inside kingdom
events.summary:
Exclusive: More than 60 accounts on X have been made unavailable in Saudi Arabia, after similar action on Snapchat and Facebook

Elon Musk’s X has become the latest major US social media company to block the accounts of Saudi Arabian dissidents so they are no longer visible inside the kingdom, following orders from Saudi authorities.

Earlier this year, the Guardian reported that platforms including Snapchat and Meta’s Facebook and Instagram had blocked dissidents’ accounts over allegations by Saudi authorities that they were violating local law.

Continue reading...

events.title: India’s ruling BJP loses byelection in stronghold after Cockroach student protests
events.summary:
Opposition parties say nationwide protests that forced resignation of education secretary are beginning to dent BJP support

India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata party has lost a byelection in a seat it had held for three decades, after the Cockroach movement student protests that have shaken Narendra Modi’s government.

Prashant Kishor, a high-profile electoral strategist turned politician, scored a breakthrough win for his fledgling Jan Suraaj (Good Governance) party in the Bankipur constituency in Patna, the capital of the eastern state of Bihar.

Continue reading...

events.title: UN experts urge Canada to protect Sikh activist amid credible threats to his life
events.summary:
Special rapporteurs say ‘transnational repression by Indian authorities’ has put Moninder Singh in danger

UN rights experts have urged Canada to take all feasible measures to protect the Sikh activist Moninder Singh, who has been repeatedly warned by the Canadian authorities of credible threats to his life.

In a letter to the Canadian government, the five UN experts raised “concerning allegations of foreign intimidation and reprisals” against Singh, a Canadian national.

Continue reading...

events.title: Red Cross visits Aung San Suu Kyi after Myanmar military pushed to prove she is alive
events.summary:
Meeting follows years of questions over wellbeing of detained former leader, who was ousted by coup in 2021

Myanmar’s detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi has met a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the aid organisation has confirmed.

The meeting on Monday ⁠followed years of questions over the wellbeing of the 81-year-old, whose whereabouts and health condition have been largely unknown since the elected civilian government she led was ousted by a military coup in February 2021.

Continue reading...

events.title: Top mountaineer Nirmal Purja confirmed dead after 11 hit by avalanche in Pakistan
events.summary:
Other members of expedition led by world-renowned climber on Broad Peak also died, climbing company says

A world-renowned Nepali mountaineer and former UK Special Forces member has died after being among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak.

Nirmal Purja was killed leading an expedition of 10 other people on the world’s 12th-highest mountain when an avalanche struck at around noon on Thursday.

Continue reading...

events.title: India’s monsoon rains in danger as UN chief warns planet is ‘on fire’
events.summary:
António Guterres says strengthening El Niño will help push the world’s climate crisis into ‘uncharted territory’

India’s monsoon is in danger and hotter, drier conditions are forecast across much of the world as a stronger El Niño weather system is taking hold, weather experts have warned.

António Guterres, the UN secretary general, said the strengthening El Niño was “adding fuel to a planet already on fire” and pushing the world into “uncharted territory”.

Continue reading...

events.title: BP boss urges Burnham to prioritise UK oil and gas even as firm exits North Sea
events.summary:
Meg O’Neill says ‘where we generate jobs, we generate tax revenue’, as company’s profits more than double

  • Revealed: major oil firms make $93bn profits amid war and climate crisis

  • Nils Pratley: BP boss is unsentimental in pruning portfolio and clear on North Sea advice to Burnham

BP’s chief executive has urged Andy Burnham to make use of the UK’s oil and gas resources even as the oil company prepares to sell its North Sea business after 60 years in the ageing basin.

In a conversation with the new prime minister, Meg O’Neill said the country should prioritise using energy produced in the UK, “where we generate jobs, we generate tax revenue, we generate all those additional positive impacts”.

Continue reading...

events.title: Dinghy carrying 173 people capsizes in Channel after engine catches fire
events.summary:
All passengers thought to have been taken to Boulogne after large air and sea rescue operation by France and UK

A dinghy carrying 173 people has capsized after its engine caught fire as it attempted to cross the Channel from France.

The people onboard were rescued from the water after a large air and sea operation was launched using UK border security and French vessels along with an RNLI boat.

Continue reading...

events.title: Calls to ban disposable barbecues in England and Wales over wildfire risk
events.summary:
Lib Dems and many Labour MPs join farmers, landowners and firefighters in urging temporary prohibition

Farmers and landowners are calling for a temporary ban on disposable barbecues in England and Wales, as they warn of the risk of igniting wildfires.

The call, which has also been made by firefighters and is backed by the Liberal Democrats and many Labour MPs, comes as much of England faces further hot dry weather, despite rain in some areas.

Continue reading...

events.title: Electronic tagging system failing to alert authorities of probation breaches, watchdog warns
events.summary:
Probation inspector for England and Wales says ‘clunky’ system needs huge increase in staff

The electronic tagging system that will be relied upon to monitor thousands of offenders released early from prison is failing to alert the authorities of potential breaches of conditions, a watchdog has warned.

Martin Jones, HM inspector of probation in England and Wales, said the system relied on hard-pressed police and probation officers looking up individual cases and then deciding whether potential breaches needed to be investigated further.

Continue reading...

events.title: Labour members ‘have tougher view on welfare than you might think’, poll suggests
events.summary:
Survey finds party members see health, the economy, cost of living and climate crisis among biggest challenges

Andy Burnham has inherited a Labour membership that is sceptical about increased welfare spending, supportive of higher defence spending, and ranks the climate crisis as one of the country’s biggest challenges, according to new polling.

The survey of 788 members between the end of June and the end of July shows them ranking health (43%), the economy (42%), cost of living (39%) and climate change (29%) as Britain’s most important issues, ahead of welfare benefits (7%) and immigration (6%).

Continue reading...

events.title: Washington state Democrat who flipped pro-Trump district faces tough primary
events.summary:
Incumbent Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, a moderate who owns an auto repair shop, hopes to retain congressional seat

The two-term Democratic congresswoman Marie Gluesenkamp Perez is heading into one of the country’s most closely watched contests on Tuesday after national recognition for flipping a Republican seat in 2022.

Representing Washington state’s third district, Gluesenkamp Perez finds herself squeezed between Democrat and progressive Brent Hennrich and Republican state senator John Braun on her right. There are six other candidates on a single crowded ballot and the top two finishers will advance to the November general election regardless of party.

Continue reading...

events.title: Devastating LA wildfire sparked by utility company tower, long-awaited report finds
events.summary:
Investigators pin blame for Eaton fire, which killed 19 people and ruined thousands of homes, on ‘electrical arcing events’ at out-of-service tower

The deadly 2025 Eaton fire in the Los Angeles area was caused by equipment belonging to the utility company Southern California Edison, fire officials said in a report released on Tuesday.

Los Angeles county fire officials found that the cause of the fire that killed 19 people and destroyed or damaged more than 9,000 homes and businesses was a tower that was not in service, according to the report.

Continue reading...

events.title: House committee launches investigation into Republican lawmaker amid domestic abuse allegations – live
events.summary:
Max Miller says he has ‘nothing to hide’ amid domestic abuse allegations made against him by his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, daughter of Republican Ohio senator Bernie Moreno

  • Sign up for US Breaking News email

The White House has called an emergency summit of artificial intelligence business leaders on Tuesday to finalize details of a voluntary compliance system for safety breaches, following reports that two major AI tools had breached their digital containment and hacked external computer systems.

Anthropic reported last week that models of its Claude tool successfully hacked into the infrastructure of three separate companies during red-teaming tests by exploiting weak passwords and unauthenticated endpoints. Anthropic said an external evaluation partner mistakenly granted the testing agent unfiltered internet access.

Continue reading...

events.title: University of Maryland ‘teacher of the year’ detained by ICE in Texas
events.summary:
DHS said pharmacy instructor Berhanu Kibret overstayed visa and arrested him at Dallas-Fort Worth airport

An instructor at the University of Maryland, Baltimore who only just received a “teacher of the year” award has been arrested by federal immigration agents under the command of the Trump administration.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials detained Berhanu Kibret, an instructor at the university’s pharmacy school, at the Dallas-Fort Worth airport in Texas, according to multiple news reports. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, confirmed Kibret’s arrest, citing an expired visa – but it stopped short of providing a location.

Continue reading...

events.title: Ex-Olympian weighing ‘all options’ after reflecting pool charges dropped
events.summary:
David Hearn has ‘number of potential remedies’ after being prosecuted in connection with pool damage, attorney says

An attorney for the former Olympic canoeist who was charged with vandalizing the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool has said that “all options are on table” for legal recourse after prosecutors recently abandoned the case abruptly.

David Hearn “has a number of potential remedies” after being prosecuted in connection with pool damage now attributed to faulty work by a contractor, attorney Steven Levin said in a statement. Levin added that those could include “civil suits, bar referrals for the prosecutors involved, request for sanctions and reimbursement of attorneys’ fees and expenses”, and requests for investigations by various government entities, including Congress.

Continue reading...

events.title: The soaring demand for Patriot missiles, from the Middle East to Ukraine
events.summary: The U.S. and its partners depend on Patriot interceptors to shoot down incoming ballistic missiles. But Russia and Iran are firing their weapons at rates far higher than Patriots can be produced.

events.summary: Europe's heat wave exposes buried history and new threats — Nazi-era wrecks emerge from the Danube, nuclear reactors face cooling risks, and Greece battles deadly wildfires.

events.summary: A woman who won €1 million mistakenly threw her lottery ticket in a trash bin in Bitonto, southern Italy — prompting her local sanitation company to launch an hourslong search.

events.summary: Tens of thousands of migrants crossed into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta several days ago. DW interviewed two experts to understand what may have caused the incident.

events.title: Middle East: India says commercial ship sunk off Yemen
events.summary: India reported an attack on a "defenseless" commercial ship which caused it to capsize and sink, but noted the crew were safe. Meanwhile, Lebanon and Israel met for talks despite Hezbollah's objections. DW has more.

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: What does Zambia's opposition stand without Edgar Lungu?
events.summary: The death of former President Edgar Lungu reshaped opposition politics in Zambia ahead of the August 13 general election. Analysts say the vote will test whether his legacy can keep opposition supporters united.

events.title: EU agrees to send border aid to Spain after Ceuta talks
events.summary: The Schengen Area was "in no way" compromised during the Ceuta incursion, Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said after a video conference with his EU colleagues.

events.summary: Two years after a student-led uprising toppled PM Sheikh Hasina, critics say Bangladesh's reform momentum is fading as political divisions deepen and key changes stall.

events.title: Guatemala: Towns evacuated as Fuego volcano erupts
events.summary: The country's disaster agency issued its second-highest warning level and urged residents to seek shelter. Onlookers have also been warned to stop climbing a nearby volcano to take videos of the eruption.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: Iran: Is Reza Pahlavi's political star fading?
events.summary: Once seen as a leading opposition figure, Pahlavi now faces questions about his political relevance in Western capitals and inside Iran.

events.title: Ukraine drone strikes kill five near Moscow, Russia says
events.summary: Russian officials say Ukrainian drones have killed five people, hitting industrial and warehouse sites near Moscow and St Petersburg. Meanwhile, a soldier has killed four people in Russian-controlled Crimea. DW has more.

events.title: South Korea: 16 dead amid record heat wave, President Lee urges action
events.summary: President Lee Jae Myung called on officials to take prompt action as extreme weather conditions became "normal." Authorities extended their first-ever heat wave warning ⁠for all of Seoul on Tuesday.

events.title: Three lions die of heatstroke at Tokyo zoo
events.summary: The zoo said that 10 of its 16 lions have been ill. Japan has been experiencing an extreme heat wave since late July.

events.title: Germany news: Hedgehog triggers police alert
events.summary: Police responding to a supermarket burglar alarm in central Germany found it was caused by an unlikely culprit. Germany's flag carrier, Lufthansa, has turned in poor quarterly results. DW has more.

events.title: India: Bangladesh presses Delhi over Sheikh Hasina speech
events.summary: Dhaka has warned New Delhi that giving a political platform to Bangladesh's former leader could hurt the improving ties between the nations. Meanwhile, Assam is reeling from devastating floods.

events.title: Venezuela earthquake death toll crosses 6,000
events.summary: The updated death toll comes weeks after the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude quakes hit on June 24, causing massive damage to people and property.

events.summary: Authorities say unfavorable weather in the Caribbean has hampered efforts to restore power to Cuba's national grid amid repeated blackouts. Many Cubans now have power only for a few hours a day.

events.title: US: 25 states sue over Trump's new tariffs
events.summary: The coalition of largely Democratic-led states is challenging the Trump administration's argument that tariffs will address imports produced by alleged "forced labor" abroad. The White House insists the move is legal.

events.title: Study shows why younger generations may be more cancer-prone
events.summary: Researchers are observing certain age-related types of cancer more frequently in younger people. A new study suggests this could be because younger generations are aging faster than their parents or grandparents.

events.title: Dry Danube River threatens nuclear power in Romania, Hungary
events.summary: Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant was operating at about 10% of capacity because of a lack of cooling river water. In Romania, the military blew up a rock outcrop in a bid to improve water flow to the Cernavoda plant.

events.title: Ceuta: EU calls borders a 'shared European responsibility'
events.summary: The European Commission has offered Morocco more support at the border to Ceuta and Melilla, and called for "united action" from the bloc on border security. Its interior ministers will discuss the issue on Tuesday.

events.title: Binging on cringe: It's as addictive as 'eating junk food'
events.summary: Flexing achievements? Cringe. Expressing genuine emotions? Cringe. You want to look away, but you can’t. Cringe. It's so addictive, people have built social media careers by monetizing other people's worst moments.

events.title: Germany news: DB hampered by 'organized irresponsibility'
events.summary: DB chief Evelyn Palla wants to overcome the culture of ''organized irresponsibility" by empowering new decision-makers within the railway operator. Bavarian brass musicians have wrapped up a 72-hour concert. DW has more.

events.title: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
events.summary: The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.

events.title: Poland: Prime Minister Tusk defies anti-Ukrainian violence
events.summary: Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.

events.title: Germany: Islamism and right-wing extremism — a story of mutual radicalization
events.summary: Following the attack on a Berlin Pride festival, the focus in Germany is turning to Islamist terrorism. An expert warns: Looking only at Islamists overlooks the parallels with right-wing extremism.

events.title: Germany: As temperatures rise, so does climate skepticism
events.summary: Some 98% of active climate scientists say climate change is happening, and is man-made. Nonetheless, a new study shows the number of climate-change skeptics in Germany has increased. Why is that?

events.title: On the front line of Europe's battle against wildfires
events.summary: French firefighters have won out over a massive blaze, with almost 200,000 evacuees returning home. But Europe's climate-fueled wildfire season is far from over.

events.title: Hungary to shut sole nuclear plant for first time on Sunday
events.summary: Record-low water levels on the Danube forced the Paks plant offline, leaving Hungary facing a potential power crunch. In neighboring Serbia, energy production at two hydroelectric plants has also been reduced.

events.title: How does eastern Europe commemorate the Roma Holocaust?
events.summary: In 2015, the EU designated August 2 as the European Roma Holocaust Memorial Day. In Germany, the day is marked with memorial services, educational activites and public addresses. And in eastern Europe?

events.title: Germany widens deportations to Afghanistan
events.summary: Earlier this week, Germany for the first time deported a man with no criminal record to Kabul. Faridoon Tofan, who is currently in deportation detention, fears the same fate.

events.title: More women die in heatwaves, but biology 'isn't main cause'

events.title: War in Ukraine: Why Crimea has become a strategic target

events.title: Germany weighs the future of minijobs
events.summary: Germany's popular minijob system allows millions of workers, including students, to avoid paying income tax or social security contributions. But a reform is on the cards that may soon end this advantage.

events.title: What's really causing Europe's wildfires
events.summary: From Greece to France, Europe is burning. But what's the real reason for the historic blazes ripping through the continent and why are they getting harder to stop?

events.title: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
events.summary: From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

events.title: Humanoid robots: Trump's latest China trade battle?
events.summary: The US has banned foreign-made humanoid robots, a market Chinese tech firms dominate. Although Washington cited national security risks, analysts think Donald Trump is buying time for US robot makers to catch up.

events.title: Eco wins: From death strip to nature haven and other green surprises
events.summary: A Cold War relic becomes a biodiversity haven, a Pokemon Go for trees and seagrass gets a second life. This week's eco wins come from some unexpected places.

events.title: FIFA plans: Infantino under pressure as senior advisor quits
events.summary: After regional football federations condemned FIFA plans for private investment, Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, tendered his resignation.

events.title: German court rules that AI music firm Suno violated copyrights
events.summary: Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, GEMA, says the verdict has "global significance," as Suno is also directed to pay yet-to-be-quantified damages.

events.title: Spain's PM visits Ceuta after thousands breached border
events.summary: Thousands of people continued pouring into Ceuta from Morocco during the night, after Spanish police lost control of the border. The head of the city government estimated that 60,000 people had entered.

events.title: Giving birth in Serbia: 'You leave your dignity at the door'
events.summary: A months-long DW investigation into childbirth in Serbia revealed a striking pattern in women's negative experiences, the widespread use of practices not universally recommended by the WHO and a system under pressure.

events.title: Spain will send troops to Ceuta to help with border security
events.summary: Authorities in the Spanish city of Ceuta asked Madrid to declare a national emergency and send military assistance. Crowds of people breached the border of the territory next to Morocco as police lost control.

events.title: Berlin Pride attack: Are German juvenile courts too lenient?
events.summary: The terror attack on Berlin Pride has put the work of juvenile courts into the spotlight. Many argue the 21-year-old perpetrator should have been in prison at the time of the attack.

events.title: BMW to Volkswagen: How deep is Germany's auto industry cull?
events.summary: BMW joins VW, Porsche and Mercedes-Benz in cutting thousands of jobs, as Chinese rivals erode their market share. DW recaps the major reforms German automakers are pursuing to safeguard their future.

events.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell-off
events.summary: Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may be ready to oppose Infantino's re-election.

events.title: Crete wildfires cause evacuations and firefighter deaths
events.summary: Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.

events.title: 'Rienzi': Why this Wagner opera is so relevant today
events.summary: The opera sparked controversy long before its Bayreuth Festival premiere, and the debate hasn't died down since it came to the stage. Now, another controversy surrounds the new AI-generated Ring cycle.

events.title: How well are LGBTQ+ rights protected across Europe?

events.summary: Germany's Muslim organizations condemn the Islamist terrorist attack targeting Berlin's Pride celebrations and fear repercussions.

events.title: Bayreuth Festival opens with celebration and commemoration
events.summary: To mark its 150th anniversary, the Bayreuth Festival remembers victims of the Holocaust — and confronts its founder's antisemitism.

events.summary: Germany has set up many programs to help individuals break away from the radical Islamist scene. Following the Islamist terror attack on Berlin's Pride event, critics say the programs are ineffective.

events.title: Germany: How weather extremes impact local agriculture
events.summary: Heat, drought, heavy rain and late frosts are taking a toll on German farmers. They increasingly respond with adapted varieties, new crops, modern breeding techniques and modified farming methods.

events.title: Why is Germany building roads for yesterday's climate?

events.title: Israel-Lebanon negotiations 'stalling': 'Situation on ground far from spirit of framework agreement'

Despite the symbolism of a seventh round of US-sponsored negotiations between Lebanon and Israel, Bahout argues that the process is increasingly characterised by stagnation rather than diplomatic momentum. He suggests that the core obstacles are no longer merely technical disagreements over the implementation of the June framework agreement, but a convergence of military realities, domestic political constraints, diminishing American engagement, and wider regional tensions. The negotiations, in his view, exist within a broader strategic ecosystem in which progress on Lebanese-Israeli arrangements remains contingent upon developments in the Iran-US war and Israeli domestic politics.

events.title: 'World's largest humanitarian crisis Thirty five million Sudanese need humanitarian assistance'

Segaar argues that the conflict can no longer be understood merely through the lens of shifting frontlines or military developments. Rather, he presents a picture of systemic societal collapse, in which war has hollowed out public services, displaced entire communities, accelerated disease, and created conditions where humanitarian need extends far beyond the active battlefields. Sudan is not simply a conflict zone but a nation experiencing the cumulative breakdown of its social, economic and institutional fabric.

events.title: Wildfire prevention requires 'nature-based solutions': Land 'treating us' the way we treat the land
events.summary: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Alexander Held, Senior Expert of the Resilience Programme for Integrated Fire Management. Held explains how Europe's escalating wildfire crisis is exposing the limits of a response model built around emergency suppression rather than long-term resilience. He argues that while the European Union has significantly improved its capacity to coordinate firefighting efforts, it continues to intervene only after the fact: once wildfires have already become uncontrollable. His central thesis is that the challenge is no longer primarily one of firefighting but of landscape governance. Climate change may intensify the conditions for extreme fires, yet the scale and destructiveness of these events are also shaped by decades of land abandonment, fuel accumulation, changing agricultural practices, and political incentives that favour highly visible emergency responses over less visible preventive measures.

events.summary: Cyberattacks targeting municipal water systems have been reported in at least seven states this week, prompting the FBI and the Environmental Protection Agency to warn utilities nationwide that hackers are trying to disrupt critical water infrastructure.

events.title: Trump calls Iranian leadership ‘extremely duplicitous’ after Tehran denies new talks will start Monday
events.summary: Iran said it wasn’t holding talks with the U.S. but was in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Video shows drone chasing Ukrainian man around van before exploding
events.summary:
Video shows drone chasing Ukrainian man around van before exploding
Ukrainian authorities have released video said to show a Russian drone being used to deliberately chase and target a civilian. The 52-year-old farmer and market trader was wounded but survived the attack.

events.title: Mourners hold a mass funeral for 112 recovered bodies in Gaza
events.summary: Mourners in Gaza held a mass funeral for 112 recovered bodies of Palestinians killed during Israeli airstrikes in 2023.

events.title: Russia says a Ukrainian drone struck a busy beach, killing at least 7 people
events.summary: Russia said that seven people, including three children, had been killed and about 40 injured in what it said was a deliberate Ukrainian drone attack on civilians.

events.title: Two killed after firefighting helicopters collide in Greece
events.summary: Two crew members were killed in a deadly mid-air crash involving two firefighting helicopters battling wildfires in Greece, according to authorities there. It comes as historic wildfires burn through parts of Europe. NBC News’ Matt Bradley reports.

events.title: East Asia is baking in ‘cruelly hot’ summer
events.summary: A deadly heat wave is gripping large parts of East Asia, bringing the hottest temperature on record in South Korea and complicating earthquake recovery efforts in Japan.

events.title: U.S. agrees to pause attacks on Iran subject to ‘rapidly’ making deal, Trump says
events.summary: The deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending Tehran’s “nuclear threat,” the president said.

events.title: At least 86 dead after migrants rush into Spanish territory from Morocco
events.summary: Spain was scrambling Friday to contain a sudden border crisis after tens of thousands of people rushed into its North African territory, with dozens killed and political shock waves spreading across Europe.

events.title: Iran vows to ‘punish the aggressor today’ after U.S. unleashes ‘heavy wave’ of strikes
events.summary: The conflict appeared to draw in new countries, as Egypt confirmed that a drone hit two natural gas vessels at one of its ports.

events.title: U.S. strikes Iran after Trump reportedly issues menacing new threat
events.summary: The fighting shattered a brief period of calm after weeks of escalation between the U.S. and Iran over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: K-pop group BTS won’t submit its music for Grammy Awards
events.summary: “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement.
